relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with SSADH deficiency and an ALDH5A1 variant: "Genetic testing revealed a homozygous mutation in the aldehyde dehydrogenase 5 family member A1 (ALDH5A1) gene."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (no tables); built the JSON with a short script in scratch and checked every span verbatim against the paper. Three in-scope people: the case-report patient ('patient'); her sibling who died at one year of a severe convulsion, untested ('sibling of patient', no variant row; included as an affected relative); and the previously published Horino et al. patient [7] in the Discussion ('ref [7] patient'), included because individual-level facts are given (age, status epilepticus, EEG, survival, regression, myoclonus, atrophy); no variant printed for that person, so no variant row. The healthy mother is not tested or affected, so no row. Sibling sex 'female' rests on the pronoun in 'She died at our hospital of respiratory failure after a prolonged convulsion ... Genetic testing was ordered for her at that time but unfortunately was not done', which follows the sibling sentence; the pronoun could be read as ambiguous. Variant printed only as genomic 'G->A substitution at chr6:24505155' with no build, transcript, cDNA or protein HGVS; the text says Akaboshi et al. 'predicted' an abnormal translation at amino acid position 223, which is a prediction cited from another paper, not an assay, so functional evidence, variant type and protein fields are left not reported/null. Normal MRI at two months ('normal cortex, white matter, cerebellum, and ventricular system'; 'normal myelination') recorded as excluded named abnormalities under D-27; the checklist item 'cerebral or cerebellar atrophy' and the T2-hyperintensity item were left not reported for the patient because the MRI statement names structures as normal rather than atrophy or basal ganglia/dentate signal. Deceased age P4M is from the title ('Four-Month-Old Infant'); exact age at death is not stated. Ref [7] patient's age 'nine-month-old' is recorded as onset of status epileptics, not as age at onset of disease. Contradictions/oddities in the paper: it calls the case 'fetal' though she is a four-month-old infant; the Discussion and Conclusions stress diagnosis 'in the absence of a familial history' while the Case presentation describes a sibling who died of a severe convulsion; midazolam dose printed as '8 mg/kg/minute'.
